summary: Tested Follow-ups 2.0 (Phase 1+2+3): configurable automation-rules API, the new Tile Selections/Tile Quotations workspace producer, workspace tabs UI, WhatsApp/Email templates, auto-close on move-to-quotation, and full regression of the pre-existing generic Follow-ups inbox. Backend: GET/PUT /api/followups/config/automation-rules works exactly as spec'd (selection [2,4,7,10], quotation_tiles [2,5,10,15], PUT updates+persists+restorable). Workspace producer correctly tags selection_waiting/quotation_tiles_waiting rows with 'TILES' and reason prefixes 'Selection '/'Quotation ', and every quotation_id resolved to a real matching tiles_selection/tiles_quotation document (verified live, not fabricated). WhatsApp contact template for a Selections card matched the exact required text byte-for-byte; Quotations card message correctly includes the quotation number. Auto-close verified live: approving + move-to-quotation on a Tile Selection with an open selection_waiting card flips it to status=done/auto_resolved=true after POST /followups/reconcile, exactly as spec'd. Frontend: 3-tab segmented control ('All'/'Selections · N'/'Quotations · N') renders with real non-zero counts, filters correctly to only TILES-tagged cards, 'Open Selection'/'Open Quotation' buttons navigate to /tiles/selection|quotation?id=<real id> and render the correct document data. Automation Rules sheet correctly lists 'Tile Selection waiting' and 'Tile Quotation waiting' alongside all pre-existing rule types. Regression of the standard inbox (Mission Hero, KPI strip, search, priority filter, category/type filter, Call/WhatsApp/Snooze/Assign actions on a NON-tiles payment_overdue card, Export, Team View) all worked with no behavioral change. Tile Orders (Customer/Brands/Dispatch List/Material Movement Register) spot-checked — loads fine, no cross-module regression. HOWEVER: found and reproduced (twice, independently) a CRITICAL concurrency/duplicate bug in reconcile_followups() — see backend_issues.critical.

critical.issue: Reconcile is NOT safe under concurrent execution: it does a read-then-write (find existing_by_key, then insert if missing) with no unique index on `source_key` and no locking/transaction. quotation_routes.py fires `asyncio.create_task(reconcile_followups())` as a fire-and-forget background task from at least 3 places (status PATCH, move-to-quotation, place-order/confirm). If a caller also awaits an explicit POST /followups/reconcile shortly after one of those actions (exactly what the review request's own auto-close test steps instruct: PATCH status=approved -> move-to-quotation -> POST /reconcile), the background task and the explicit call can both run reconcile_followups() concurrently. Both instances query `existing_by_key` before either has inserted, both find the key missing, and both insert — producing two OPEN `is_automated=true` rows with the IDENTICAL `source_key` (e.g. `quotation_tiles_waiting:<qid>`) for the same quotation. Reproduced live twice on two different quotations (1209b0ed-...-...944 and e119aac8-...-...c8) using nothing but the exact API sequence described in the review request's auto-close test. This directly violates the code's own documented idempotency guarantee ('re-running it never duplicates a card — dedupe key = source_key'). Regression-guard pytest added: test_no_duplicate_source_keys_for_tiles_rules (currently FAILING against live data).

minor.issue: Pre-existing (not introduced this session) integration test tests/integration/test_followups_v2.py::test_order_confirm_and_payment_and_dispatch_trigger_reconcile fails with KeyError: 'purchase_orders' — the endpoint's response shape (`{quotation_id, idempotent, **result}` from dispatch_event) no longer includes a top-level `purchase_orders` key that an earlier test version expected. Unrelated to Follow-ups 2.0 scope; flagging so it isn't lost.

action_items: PRIORITY: Fix the reconcile_followups() race condition. Recommended: add a unique Mongo index on followups.source_key (partial/sparse, since manual rows have source_key=None) and change the persist loop to use a true atomic upsert (update_one(..., upsert=True) keyed on source_key) instead of find-then-insert, OR wrap reconcile_followups() in a mutex/distributed lock keyed by a fixed name so overlapping calls serialize. Also consider NOT firing reconcile as a bare asyncio.create_task from quotation_routes.py right before callers might independently trigger their own reconcile (e.g. the frontend's bootstrap() already fires one on every Follow-ups page load) — at minimum, awaiting it (or debouncing) would close this specific window.
After the fix, re-run backend/tests/integration/test_followups_v2_workspaces.py::TestWorkspaceProducer::test_no_duplicate_source_keys_for_tiles_rules — it will fail again if the race still exists.

rca_of_issue: Root cause: reconcile_followups() (services/followup_engine.py) computes a `desired` dict keyed by source_key, then for each key does `ex = existing_by_key.pop(key, None)` against a snapshot of existing automated rows fetched via ONE query at the top of the function — if `ex` is None it inserts a brand-new Followup document. There is no unique database constraint on `source_key` and no locking around this check-then-act sequence. Three routes in routes/quotation_routes.py (PATCH status change, move-to-quotation, place-order/confirm) each fire `asyncio.create_task(reconcile_followups())` as a fire-and-forget background task — meaning the HTTP response returns before that reconcile pass necessarily completes. The review request's own prescribed auto-close test sequence (PATCH status=approved -> POST move-to-quotation -> POST /followups/reconcile) triggers exactly this: move-to-quotation's background reconcile and the immediately-following explicit reconcile call both start with the same stale `existing_by_key` snapshot (neither sees the other's in-flight insert), both compute the same new `quotation_tiles_waiting:<qid>` key as 'not existing', and both insert a row — yielding 2 OPEN, is_automated=true, identical-source_key duplicates. This is a genuine, deterministic-under-the-right-timing concurrency bug, not a flaky test artifact (reproduced on 2 separate quotations across 2 separate test runs).
